Teaching philosophy

Complex ideas, built up in clear steps and tested in practice

I teach fast-moving subjects like AI and cybersecurity by connecting each concept to something students can run, break and explain for themselves.

Structure first

Modules are organised into clear learning pathways aligned with UK learning outcomes, so students always know what they are building towards.

Learn by doing

Every session includes hands-on work in Python and Google Colab, from regression models to forensic evidence analysis.

Industry grounded

Two years as a software developer in Agile teams shapes how I teach design, testing and debugging as real professional practice.

Feedback and mentoring

Structured formative and summative feedback, plus one-to-one mentoring, supports every student from proposal to finished project.

Teaching areas

Two specialist tracks

Specialist teaching in AI and cybersecurity, built on a broad computer science foundation.

Track A

AI & Cybersecurity

  • Digital forensics and digital investigations
  • Cybercrime analysis and information security fundamentals
  • Machine learning and AI in security applications
  • Explainable AI (LIME, SHAP) for security systems
  • Research methods: systematic literature review, statistical testing
TensorFlowscikit-learnGoogle ColabLIME / SHAP

Track B

Computer Science

  • Programming in Python, Java, C#, C, C++ and SQL
  • Database systems: relational design, MySQL, SQL Server, query optimisation
  • Software engineering: OOP, SDLC, system design, Agile
  • Networking: OSI and TCP/IP, subnetting, routing and switching
  • Applied AI and data science
JavaPythonMySQLTCP/IP

Across both tracks: delivery on UK-awarding-body validated programmes (Pearson HND, remote BSc/MSc), assessment and coursework design, LMS-based online and blended teaching, and student project supervision from proposal to implementation.
